subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact lava golem module with a biped skeleton including hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, arms, and IK legs, aiming to keep the code around 250 lines using toon-style cel shading for a basalt look.

I'm laying out the hip and spine chain joints with coordinates, building the torso with a swept loft shape, then adding glowing lava cracks and basalt plate details scattered across the chest surface.

For the head I'm planning a boxy sphere shape with glowing eye planes, a separate lava-mouth jaw, basalt horns, and flame card crowns, plus a neck joint; for the arms I'm setting up oversized shoulder-to-wrist IK chains with swept limb geometry and chunky fist/finger boxes at the wrists.

Now I'm adding hex-cylinder pauldrons on the shoulders, IK leg chains from hip to foot with box feet, spine-mounted lava vent spikes, and a jawbone piece with teeth, while working out left/right mirroring via a side multiplier before writing the actual part-placement code.

Placing the head and neck joints using model-space coordinates to avoid local-axis confusion, then building the head as a chamfered box with a brow ridge and glowing eye planes positioned just above center.

Working out the jaw joint and geometry with a lava-colored glow slab for the mouth interior and small teeth cones, keeping the jaw as a separate basalt-textured piece from the glowing inner slab.

For horns, I'm using spike geometry swept from the head top with mirrored directions for symmetry, then building a flame mohawk using card meshes arranged along a frame path, applying a glow effect to the resulting flame meshes.

Now I'm building the torso using a swept chain from hips to chest tip with a tapering radius function, adding a separate pelvis box piece at the hips, and scattering hexagonal plate meshes across the torso surface for armor detailing.

For the core glow, I'm placing a small icosahedron at the chest with emissive glow, then surrounding it with a ring of eight spike-like plates radiating outward using box geometry stuck to a radial frame.

I'm recalculating the torso's front-facing z-offset since the ellipse radius differs by axis, so I'm nudging the core position to around z=0.42 so it sits half-embedded in the chest rather than buried inside. For the legs, I'm defining a limb chain with named joints (hip, knee, ankle) and tapering sweep radii for the thigh segment.

Now I'm setting foot box dimensions and positions so they align with the ankle bone target height, double-checking the bottom of the foot touches y=0, then placing knee plates and considering lava-crack texturing for the feet. For the arms, I'm positioning the shoulder and hand joints with bent elbow direction pointing backward to get a natural arm pose.

Checking the shoulder-to-hand reach distance, I realize the arm segments come up short so I'm adjusting the bone lengths to cover it properly, while confirming the fist stays above the floor and total golem height caps around 3 meters. I'm also writing a paint function for lava cracks using cell-based noise to blend hot colors along cell boundaries.

Defining a reusable basalt cel-shaded material for cracks and a separate plate material with its own color variation, keeping lava glow parts as flat colors for performance.

I'm skipping floating ember particles for now and instead adding back spikes along the torso spine using surface positioning, with lava-tipped basalt cones decreasing in size. For the eyes and flames I'm sketching simple SVG shapes—an angled angry eye with a hot white core, and a teardrop flame with gradient fill—before moving into writing the actual torso sweep code.

Adding plate scatter filters...
